subject: Urgent: Southcentral AZ2 blackout — recovery coordination & exec update
messages:
From: Samantha Cho <samantha@pioneerhealth.io>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-10-14T08:02:00-07:00
Subject: API failures — huge latency + 502 spike in Southcentral AZ2

Rachel —

We started seeing a severe spike in 5xxs and token-level latency in our production environment around 07:40 PT. Error rate rose from ~0.2% to ~18% and tail latency jumped >5s for many endpoints. Traffic is primarily routed to Southcentral AZ2 (our pinned region). This is causing timeouts for our interactive clinician workflows.

We opened an incident on our side and moved a small subset of traffic to USW2, which helped some sessions, but the bulk of our users remain impacted. Can you confirm whether this is a regional outage on Redwood's side or if there's a configuration we missed? We need an ETA and whether you can perform an emergency cross-region failover for us (we're on a dedicated pool).

This is P0 for us — customers are on the phone. Please escalate to engineering and leadership.

— Samantha
Samantha Cho
Head of Platform Engineering, Pioneer Health
ops@pioneerhealth.io

Attachments: none
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Cho <samantha@pioneerhealth.io>
Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, jordan.blake@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-10-14T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: API failures — huge latency + 502 spike in Southcentral AZ2

Samantha — thanks for the heads up and really sorry for the disruption. We're treating this as P0.

Quick notes: we see a service degradation impacting AZ2 in Southcentral (partner cloud region). Early telemetry shows elevated queue depths and KV cache eviction thrashing on the dedicated pool serving your account which is increasing per-request latency and leading to 502 responses.

Immediate steps I have requested from SRE/infra team (see bridge):
- Open bridge and fail traffic to the nearest compatible model variant in USW2 (canary shift 20% immediately, then scale if stable)
- Temporarily relax frontend token limits for Pioneer Health to reduce retry storms (30m window)
- Disable aggressive prefix caching to avoid cache thrash while we stabilize KV backends

Can you confirm whether Pioneer Health can accept a controlled cross-region shift to USW2 for up to 2 hours while we stabilize AZ2? We will provide a post-incident credit proposal and a short exec note once we have an initial RCA.

Bridge: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-4982 (join for live updates)

I'll stay on this thread and keep you updated every 30 minutes.

— Rachel Kim
Account Exec (Strategic Accounts) | Redwood Inference

On Sat, Oct 14, 2028 at 08:12 AM Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Samantha — thanks for the heads up and really sorry for the disruption. We're treating this as P0.

Current technical summary (08:23 PT):
- Primary symptom: sustained increase in request queue depth on the dedicated pool for Pioneer Health in Southcentral AZ2 beginning ~07:36 PT.
- Observed behavior: KV store (local sharded cache) is experiencing eviction storms under the current sequence-length distribution, causing repeated full-cache misses and heavier upstream model loads. This amplifies per-token CPU/GPU pressure and produces 502s from the GPU workers.
- Correlation: Edge telemetry shows a surge of retry traffic from a small client subset with aggressive client-side retry logic around 07:35 which coincides with the initial uptick.

Immediate actions executed:
1) Began controlled traffic steering: +20% to USW2 for Pioneer Health at 08:20 PT (canary). Telemetry shows 50% reduction in error rate for canary sessions.
2) Disabled prefix eviction aggressor and applied conservative KV retention policy to reduce thrash (rolling change completed 08:22 PT).
3) Increased SLO-based worker spawn for Pioneer dedicated pool (adds capacity while backend warms).

Requests / asks:
- Approval to broaden failover to 60% traffic to USW2 for 30 minutes to protect live clinician sessions. We will revert traffic as soon as AZ2 throughput stabilizes and caches warm.
- Marissa: can you coordinate comms with Pioneer support and give them the expected experience for shifted sessions?
- Rachel / Jordan: executive note and approval for a good‑will credit (estimated $xxk) for the impacted window. Legal will require decision to trigger credit.

Attachments: sre-bridge-logs.zip (bridge logs + time series snapshots), traffic-redirect-plan.md

Status: bridge active — http://incident.redwood/bridge/SUP-4982 (internal)

— Hannah Schmitt
Senior SRE | Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.ai, hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-10-14T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Exec summary & action items — Pioneer Health AZ2 blackstart recovery

Team —

Thanks for the fast response and the bridge work today. This is an executive-facing summary and set of asks to finalize customer comms and follow-up: 

Situation (short): Southcentral AZ2 experienced a localized outage starting ~07:36 PT caused by KV cache eviction amplification combined with a retry storm from a subset of Pioneer Health traffic. This produced elevated tail latency and 5xx spikes impacting interactive clinician workflows.

Containment we performed:
- Canary traffic shift to USW2 at 08:20 PT, scaled to 60% at 08:40 PT to protect live traffic; error rates for canary sessions dropped ~60%
- Applied KV retention policy and slowed eviction aggressors; worker autoscale increased capacity on dedicated pool
- Short token-limit relax for Pioneer to blunt client retries (30m window)

Customer impact: 07:36–09:15 PT for full userbase; partial mitigation by 08:40 PT for canary group; some sessions still experienced >3s tail latency until 09:25 PT. Pioneer escalated to execs during the event.

Required exec decisions / asks:
1) Approve $12,500 good‑will credit to Pioneer Health (estimation) to expedite renewal conversation and acknowledge impact. Legal has the draft credit memo ready.
2) Greenlight prep of a joint customer postmortem and a 1x remediation window where we will perform a cache configuration tune and run a controlled load test to validate KV retention changes. Proposed date: 2028-10-21 09:00 PT.
3) Approve a short-term SLA exception to allow temporary cross-region routing for Pioneer for up to 72h if they request (we need legal/finance consent).

Next steps: Rachel — please send a concise customer-facing note (what happened, what we did, next steps, credit) by EOD. Marissa — coordinate the customer call and send the invite for the postmortem. Hannah / Aditya — finish the RCA draft and attach the logs to the postmortem doc.

Attachments: postmortem-draft.pdf

— Jordan Blake
VP, Customer Success & Escalations | Redwood Inference
